statements.impact_statement: CVE-2002-1976 in net-tools 2.10-0.1+deb12u2: ifconfig, when used on the Linux kernel 2.2 and later, does not report when the network interface is in promiscuous mode if it was put in promiscuous mode using PACKET_MR_PROMISC, which could allow attackers to sniff the network without detection, as demonstrated using libpcap. Evidence read with image-files from the pinned image (sha256:4177c77b). The mount pod runs 'sh -c' (dash) with /usr/local/bin/juicefs format and then exec /bin/mount.juicefs (symlink to juicefs); the image has no ENTRYPOINT and a bash CMD that the pod command replaces; the other programs the image's jobs and hooks start are fusermount, umount, rm and rmdir (source: juicefs v1.4.2 cmd/ and pkg/ exec calls; csi-driver v0.34.0 pkg/juicefs/mount/builder command strings). ELF DT_NEEDED: juicefs links libfdb_c (foundationdb-clients), librados2, libgfapi0 and libc; dash and fusermount3 link libc only; umount links libmount1 and libc. The Depends closure of those packages in /var/lib/dpkg/status has 65 of 287 packages and does not contain net-tools. The package is installed but no process in the mount pod or its jobs loads or runs it.

CVE-2026-33814 in golang.org/x/net v0.52.0: the HTTP/2 transport loops writing CONTINUATION frames when a peer sends SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE 0, so a hostile server hangs the client. Checked with govulncheck v1.10.0 in source mode (go1.25.14, linux/amd64, cgo, tags ceph,fdb,gluster) on github.com/juicedata/juicefs at 46af7afa9f81, the clean revision recorded in /usr/local/bin/juicefs of the pinned image (sha256:4177c77b); workflow run https://github.com/cthtrifork/talos-gitops/actions/runs/45971803567. The flaw is client side and needs an HTTP/2 peer. HTTP/2 is only negotiated over TLS (ALPN) or h2c, and the code has no h2c: the S3 endpoint is plain HTTP, so Go speaks HTTP/1.1 to it, and the only TLS peer is Postgres, which is not HTTP. Deployment (k8s/apps/juicefs-system/external-secrets.yaml): metaurl is postgres://juicefs@juicefs-meta-rw...:5432 with sslmode=verify-full and sslrootcert=/etc/juicefs-pg/ca.crt, storage is s3 with bucket http://garage.juicefs-system.svc:3900/juicefs (plain HTTP); the mount pod runs only 'juicefs format' and 'mount.juicefs'. The CiliumNetworkPolicy juicefs-csi allows egress only to garage:3900, juicefs-meta:5432 and the node kubelet port, and ingress only from host and remote-node. The peers are a fixed set the policy names; none speaks HTTP/2 to this pod.

The callers of ServeContent in this binary are the x/net WebDAV handler (pkg/fs/http.go newWebdavHandler, started only by StartHTTPServer from cmd/webdav.go:100) and the minio gateway file handler (cmd/gateway.go); format and mount start neither. The mount pod's listeners are the metrics http.Serve on a plain net.Listen tcp socket (cmd/mount.go:131) and the debug agent http.ListenAndServe on loopback (cmd/main.go:336); there is no tls.Listen, ServeTLS or h2c outside pkg/fs/http.go (WebDAV, started only from cmd/webdav.go:100) and the sync cluster mode, which this pod does not run. The example trace goes through the failpoint library's http.Serve in an init, which only listens when GO_FAILPOINTS_HTTP is set (failpoints.go init; the pod environment has no such variable) and then serves its own HttpHandler, not a file handler.

CVE-2026-78669 in golang.org/x/net v0.52.0: a malicious HTTP/2 peer opens many streams and floods small SETTINGS frames with SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE, causing CPU exhaustion in the client or server. The CiliumNetworkPolicy juicefs-csi allows egress only to garage:3900, juicefs-meta:5432 and the node kubelet port, and ingress only from host and remote-node.
